This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon. Federal agents searched the Washington, D.C. home of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar this morning.
As NPR's Barbara Sprunt reports, the Minnesota Democrat is a sharp critic and frequent target of President Trump.
The Department of Justice says agents with Homeland Security Investigations were executing a judicially authorized search warrant and that it's part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation.
A spokesperson for the Congresswoman calls the search a "outrageous abuse of power" and an "unprecedented escalation in the weaponization of federal law enforcement to target political enemies."
The search took place ahead of next month's midterm elections, in which Omar is seeking re-election.
Vice President Vance has previously alleged Omar committed immigration fraud, something she denies. Barbara Sprunt, NPR News, Washington.
Many leaders of Native American tribal nations are raising concerns about the Trump administration's proposal for unprecedented changes to the next U.S. census.
The census would reshape voting maps and determine how federal funding is distributed across the country. NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports.
One proposed change is not to use the 2030 census to produce statistics about race and ethnicity.
A topic has been part of the U.S. headcount since the first one in 1790. Trump officials say they see a "reduced need" for that information, which is used for redistricting and enforcing civil rights laws.
Meghan Bishop of the National Congress of American Indians is an enrolled citizen of the native village of Afognac in Alaska.
There's a significant concern about how federal funding would be distributed through grants and other programs to tribes if that race-ethnicity census question is erased.
The public can comment on their proposal through November 2nd. Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
Medicare open enrollment begins October 15th. It's a chance for people over the age of 65 to switch their coverage plans.
As NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin reports, premiums are going up for Medicare next year, much like in all health insurance plans across the country.
About half of the 66 million people enrolled in Medicare are in what's called "traditional Medicare" run by the federal government.
The other half are enrolled in Medicare Advantage, where private companies manage the plan.
Health experts say it's especially important for people enrolled in Medicare Advantage plans or prescription drug plans to log in during open enrollment and make sure your plan still fits your needs.
There are tools online at Medicare.gov for comparing options, and there are state health insurance assistance programs, or SHPs, in every state, staffed by experts who can walk people through their options and help them enroll.
Open enrollment runs through December 7th, and coverage begins January 1st.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News.
If you're enrolling in Medicare for the first time, your window opens three months before you turn 65.
You're listening to NPR News.
American-born economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford have won the Nobel Prize in Economics.
Woodford says he and Hall created an approved model that took into account how consumers and businesses made key economic decisions on how to invest and how to spend.
My work has stressed that the understanding of the people who are in the markets and making decisions about spending and so on, that their expectations and their understanding of what policy is likely to be like in the future,
are actually crucial to the effects of policy.
Woodford is associated with Columbia University. Hall is affiliated with Stanford.
Pope Leo is set to have surgery this week to remove a growth on his lung.
And Perez Eva Pukach reports lung nodules are common in older adults.
Dr. Panicky Scoliosatos, a pulmonary physician at Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, says the majority of lung nodules are benign, calling them the lung's wrinkles.
He says once a nodule is discovered, doctors then test it to see if there is cause for concern.
For the Pope to have had some imaging done that found him to have a lung nodule where they're now discussing removing it means he likely had some findings that resulted in some level of concern outside of the size.
The Vatican says the surgery will occur at Rome's Jamili Hospital and the Pope will have a week of recovery. Eva Pukach, NPR News.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.
